function: Joint learned BS transmit beamforming and RIS phase-shift configuration to maximize UE rate fairness and SC load balancing (p. 8)
system: Downlink MISO HetNet: 6 GHz macro BS, three 28 GHz small-cell BSs, 8-antenna ULAs, single-antenna UEs, passive reflecting RIS (16 elements) at each BS (p. 11)
method: DDPG-based multi-task deep RL, one actor-critic per task (3 SC fairness tasks, 1 MC load-balancing task), reinforcement learning from past-rate feedback (p. 7)
data_channel: Custom simulation: LoS wideband block-fading channels with log-distance path loss, log-normal shadowing and array steering vectors; no standardized model, dataset or measurement (p. 4)
test_conditions: Train/test on one simulated layout (3 SCs, 5 UEs each); UEs then move every 500 episodes (1-5 m/s) and the agent re-adapts (p. 13)
baselines: Non-learned: genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO). Learned: authors' earlier one-tier-RIS MTDRL with full CSI [1] (p. 11)
metrics: Log-rate utility of fairness and load-balancing tasks, per-UE and per-SC downlink rate, utility CDF over 100 realizations, convergence episodes (p. 12)
complexity: Complexity order O(KUM(phi0*phin+sum(phin*phin+1))+|S|^2*A) for the MTDRL scheme; no FLOPs, parameter count or runtime reported (p. 11)
q1_support: p. 4: "wideband block-fading channels that follow line-of-sight (LoS) model"; custom LoS simulator with path loss and shadowing, no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "UEs move every 500 episodes in random directions within their serving SCs"; p. 14: "around four times faster than the convergence speed at the initial training"
q3_support: p. 12: "is 51.18 compared to 49.33 and 47.92 for the GA and PSO solutions"; p. 11: "Our previous work in [1], where we deployed only one tier of RISs at the sub-6GHz" (learned MTDRL benchmark); p. 12: "3.65 % compared with the case when deploying RIS at the sub-6GHz only as in [1]"
q4_support: p. 11: "the complexity order of our proposed MTDRL scheme is expressed as" O(KUM(phi0*phin+sum(phin*phin+1))+|S|^2*A), in Section III-E.
q5_support: p. 11: "The DDPG-based MTDRL agent is simulated in Python with the Pytorch library"; the environment is a custom simulation and no code or data link is given anywhere.
notes: Include, area 3: the learned DDPG agent outputs BS beamformers and RIS phase shifts (p. 8); UE association is fixed (constraint C6, p. 5), so not above PHY. Tables III and IV (pp. 11-12) were read from page images. q2 is borderline: it rests on the online re-adaptation after UE mobility within the same cells and the same LoS model (pp. 13-14), not on a held-out test set. q3 is borderline: GA and PSO are the non-learned baselines (p. 11); the learned baseline is the authors' earlier MTDRL of [1] (one-tier RIS, full CSI), but the figures label it 'WO SCs RISs [1]' (p. 12), which a stricter reading may treat as an ablation of the proposed system. The reviewer should confirm both.
